=== CALL C0063 ===
Lee: Hello. Can you hear me all right?
Darren: Yeah, I can hear you. You alright?
Lee: Not bad, thanks. Lee.
Darren: Darren. Alright, mate.
Lee: Er, so I suppose we just chat, do we?
Darren: That's what it said. Three minutes.
Lee: Right. Where are you based, then?
Darren: Maidstone. Kent. You?
Lee: Hucknall. Just north of Nottingham.
Darren: Yeah, I know roughly. Never been, mind.
Lee: Not many people have, to be fair. What do you do?
Darren: Bins. Refuse and recycling, for the contractor that does the council rounds. Eleven years on and off. Six o'clock start, so I'm usually knackered by about now.
Lee: Six. That's early.
Darren: Up at five. You get used to it. Dog's not keen though. What about you?
Lee: Er, I'm a quality technician. Aerospace components, so machined parts. I check them on a measuring machine, a CMM, and write up the reports if something's out of tolerance. And I look after the calibration records.
Darren: So you're the one that tells people they've done it wrong.
Lee: Sort of, yeah. More or less. I've got two junior inspectors as well.
Darren: Same as me with the new lads, then. They skip half a road and leave the bags split all over the pavement, and then guess who gets the phone call.
Lee: Yeah. It's the same principle, I'd say. If it's not done properly it comes back on you.
Darren: Exactly that.
Lee: How long have you been there? Sorry, you said eleven years.
Darren: Eleven, yeah. You?
Lee: Nineteen at this place. One firm before that. Started as an apprentice at sixteen.
Darren: Nineteen years. Fair play. That puzzle bit at the start, I bet you was good at that, then.
Lee: Er, I got most of them. One I didn't finish in time. Annoyed me a bit, to be fair.
Darren: I gave up on the last one. Couldn't see the point.
Lee: Do you follow football at all?
Darren: Gillingham. Which is, you know. Suffering, basically. Go a few times a season with a mate.
Lee: Notts County, me. So I know the feeling.
Darren: Yeah, you lot have had it rough an' all.
Lee: We've had our moments. I don't get to Meadow Lane as much now. Mostly the radio or the app.
Darren: Same. Highlights and the darts, that's me most weekends.
Lee: Do you play? Darts.
Darren: Pub league, Thursdays. I'm alright at it. Nothing special.
Lee: I used to play cricket, village side. Gave up in my forties. Now it's walking, and the allotment.
Darren: Allotment. What d'you grow?
Lee: Runner beans did well this year. Potatoes, onions, bit of everything. I keep a planting plan written out.
Darren: Course you do.
Lee: Well. It saves guessing.
Darren: Fair enough. I just keep the back garden tidy. Can't be doing with veg. Holidays, you go away much?
Lee: Same caravan park near Mablethorpe, every year. Just me and the wife now.
Darren: Caravan in Norfolk, us. Or Benidorm if Tracey gets her way. I hate airports, mind. All that queuing.
Lee: We did Majorca once, for our anniversary. It was better than I thought. But Mablethorpe's easier.
Darren: Yeah. You know where you are with a caravan.
Lee: You do, yeah. Do you listen to much music on the rounds?
Darren: Classic rock in the van. Saw Status Quo once, years back.
Lee: Did you? I've got them on in the car most days.
Darren: Good band. Bit of Dire Straits an' all.
Lee: That's me, yeah. Funny, that.

=== CALL C0064 ===
Jasmine: Hi, can you hear me okay?
Gareth: Yeah, loud and clear. Gareth.
Jasmine: Jasmine. Hi.
Gareth: Nice cat, by the way. I saw it in the photo. Half a cat, anyway.
Jasmine: Oh, Biscuit, yeah. She's somewhere knocking things off the counter, probably. Where are you?
Gareth: Walthamstow. North-east London. You?
Jasmine: Plymouth.
Gareth: Long way off. What d'you do down there?
Jasmine: I own two bubble tea shops in the city centre. Franchise ones. I'm the director, so I do the rotas, the stock orders, the books, talk to the suppliers. I've got a supervisor full-time for the day-to-day, so I only do about twelve hours a week, which is how I like it, to be fair.
Gareth: Twelve hours. That's a sort of dream setup, isn't it.
Jasmine: Took a lot to get there. First one was 2019, then the second in 2022. What about you?
Gareth: Structural engineer. Consultancy in Farringdon. Mostly residential conversions, some commercial refurbs. Basically working out whether your loft conversion's going to fall through the ceiling.
Jasmine: And does it?
Gareth: Not if I've done it. Er, the architects try their best though. I've just had to redo a whole set of calcs because one of them moved a wall. Didn't tell anyone.
Jasmine: That's annoying.
Gareth: Yeah, a bit.
Jasmine: Do you own your place, then? Since you know about buildings.
Gareth: Nah. Renting. One-bed in a Victorian conversion. Landlord's been promising to fix the bathroom extractor fan for two years.
Jasmine: Two years? You should hold back the rent, honestly.
Gareth: Probably should. Can't be bothered with the fight, really.
Jasmine: I would. I read every clause in my leases. Landlords will try it on if you let them.
Gareth: You sound like you enjoy that bit.
Jasmine: Bit, yeah. I like a good haggle. Suppliers as well. Erm, we rent too, me and my partner, but I'm always on Rightmove. I want a couple of buy-to-lets eventually.
Gareth: London numbers just annoy me. I look and then I close the app.
Jasmine: Plymouth's much better, to be fair. You'd get a whole house for your one-bed.
Gareth: Yeah, and then I'd live in Plymouth.
Jasmine: Hey. It's nice. The Hoe, Wembury, the sea.
Gareth: Fair enough, I've never been. Do you actually drink the bubble tea?
Jasmine: Not that much anymore. When you do the stock count every week you go off it, lah. Brown sugar one is still good though.
Gareth: I've never had one. The balls put me off, sort of a texture thing.
Jasmine: Everyone says that. Then they try it and they come back every week.
Gareth: That's the business model, is it?
Jasmine: Basically, yeah. I want a third one, maybe in Exeter. Without working more hours.
Gareth: Good luck with that. I'd like fewer hours and no timesheets. Thought about going freelance.
Jasmine: Why don't you?
Gareth: Er, haven't got round to it. Bit of a pattern, to be honest.
Jasmine: You just register a company, it's not hard. Takes like twenty minutes on Companies House.
Gareth: It's the bit after the twenty minutes I'm worried about.
Jasmine: Clients, yeah. That's the actual work.
Gareth: Exactly. And I'm told I'm a bit blunt with clients.
Jasmine: Blunt's fine. I'm blunt with my staff. They still turn up.
Gareth: Mostly, yeah?
Jasmine: Except Saturdays. Someone always calls in sick on a Saturday, I swear. It's—

=== CALL C0065 ===
Darren: Alright. Can you hear me?
Bianca: Yeah. Hiya.
Darren: Darren.
Bianca: Bianca.
Darren: Where are you, then?
Bianca: Wolverhampton. Well, Bilston, kind of just outside.
Darren: Maidstone, me. Kent.
Bianca: Oh right.
Darren: What d'you do?
Bianca: Erm, I'm at uni. Second year, Accounting and Finance, at Wolverhampton.
Darren: Accounting. Sensible.
Bianca: Yeah, that's kind of why I picked it. It pays, and there's always jobs, do you know what I mean. I'm not like, passionate about it.
Darren: Fair enough. Most people aren't passionate about their job, to be fair.
Bianca: What do you do?
Darren: Bins. Loader on the council rounds. Six o'clock start.
Bianca: Oh, my boyfriend does early ones as well. Well, nights mostly. He's at a warehouse off the M6.
Darren: Nights is worse. I couldn't do nights.
Bianca: He's knackered all the time. But it means I get the flat to myself, so.
Darren: Every cloud.
Bianca: Yeah, basically.
Darren: You go in every day, to uni?
Bianca: Most days. Bus into the city campus. It was late again this morning, like twenty minutes. Nearly missed my seminar.
Darren: We get people moaning at us about being late. It's never us, it's the parked cars. You can't get the wagon down half the roads round here, people park either side, and then they ring up and say we skipped them.
Bianca: Do people ring up a lot?
Darren: All the time. And the recycling, mate. People put anything in. Nappies. Garden hoses.
Bianca: Hoses?
Darren: Wrapped round the bin drum. Twice this month.
Bianca: That's grim.
Darren: It is what it is.
Bianca: Do you like it, though? Like, the job.
Darren: It's alright. I've never missed a start in eleven years. Wouldn't say I like it. My back don't like it, put it that way.
Bianca: Eleven years without missing one? That's kind of impressive.
Darren: Just get up and go. My missus is in care, she does worse hours than me.
Bianca: Oh, my mum did care homes. When I was little. Like, long shifts, nights, weekends, all of it.
Darren: Tracey says it's harder than bins. She's probably right.
Bianca: My mum used to come in and just fall asleep on the settee. In her uniform. That's partly why I'm doing accounting, tbh. I don't want to be skint like that, do you know what I mean.
Darren: Yeah. I get that.
Bianca: Not being funny about care work. It's just a lot for not much.
Darren: No, it is. They don't pay them enough. Never have.
Bianca: Mm.
Darren: You from Wolverhampton originally, then?
Bianca: Erm, Romania originally, but I came over when I was eight. So basically from Wolves now.
Darren: You've got the accent and everything.
Bianca: Yeah, people don't believe me.
Darren: You go back?
Bianca: Most summers, to see my nan. Fly from Birmingham. I'd rather go somewhere with a nice hotel though, to be honest. Like Dubai.
Darren: Not me. Can't stand airports. All that standing about.
Bianca: I just bring a bigger bag than you're allowed and hope.
Darren: Ha. Does that work?
Bianca: Mostly. We was nearly caught once, but—

=== CALL C0066 ===
Jasmine: Hi, can you hear me?
Lee: Yes, I can. Hello. Lee.
Jasmine: Jasmine. Hi Lee.
Lee: Where are you calling from?
Jasmine: Plymouth. You?
Lee: Hucknall, near Nottingham.
Jasmine: Okay. I like your background, by the way. Very organised. The folders by year.
Lee: Er, thank you. Habit, really. I'm in quality, so it sort of comes with the job.
Jasmine: What's quality, like inspection?
Lee: Yes. Aerospace parts. I measure them on a CMM, that's a coordinate measuring machine, and if something's out of spec I write it up. And I keep the calibration records. When there's an audit coming, they tend to come to me.
Jasmine: Honestly, you looked like an accountant in your photo. You'd get on with my accountant.
Lee: I do the household budget in Excel, so maybe.
Jasmine: Proper. I do my books in Xero. I've got two bubble tea shops, franchise ones, in the city centre.
Lee: Two. How long have you had them?
Jasmine: First one 2019, then 2022 the second. I want a third, maybe Exeter.
Lee: That's a fair bit of risk, I'd say.
Jasmine: Bit, yeah. One nearly closed one winter. It was really slow, January, February, nobody wants cold drinks. I was more worried than I told anyone, to be fair. But it came back. Summer saved it.
Lee: Seasonal, then.
Jasmine: Very. You can forecast it, though. I do the stock by the weather, basically.
Lee: That's sensible.
Jasmine: Do you do audits yourself, or they audit you?
Lee: They audit us. Customer audits, and the certification body. Last one was March. Sorry, April. Early April.
Jasmine: And you pass?
Lee: We passed, yes. No major findings.
Jasmine: I'd hate that. Somebody going through all my paperwork.
Lee: It's fine if it's done properly in the first place.
Jasmine: That's the thing. Mine's mostly done properly.
Lee: Mostly.
Jasmine: Mostly, lah. Nobody checks the cleaning log for the fridges, you know.
Lee: Somebody will, one day.
Jasmine: Yeah, yeah. Okay. You sound like my supervisor. Do you have kids?
Lee: Two. My son's twenty-four, he's in Arnold with his girlfriend. My daughter's twenty, she's at university in Sheffield.
Jasmine: Oh nice. What's she studying?
Lee: Er, psychology. She comes back some weekends. House is quiet when she's not there, to be fair. We've turned my son's old room into an office.
Jasmine: That's where you are now?
Lee: That's where I am now, yes.
Jasmine: I came here for uni as well. From Malaysia, when I was eighteen. My mum was worried the whole time. She still calls every Sunday.
Lee: I'd say that's normal. You don't stop worrying.
Jasmine: She'd agree with you. Do you go away much?
Lee: Static caravan, near Mablethorpe. Same park every year.
Jasmine: Every year? I couldn't. I like all-inclusive. Tenerife, Turkey. Pool, nice hotel, don't have to cook.
Lee: We did Majorca for our twenty-fifth. It was nice. But you know where everything is at the caravan.
Jasmine: Fair. I get that. Same as going back home, I suppose.
Lee: Yes. Sort of the same thing.

=== CALL C0068 ===
Jasmine: Hi, can you hear me?
Darren: Yeah. Alright. Darren.
Jasmine: Jasmine. Where are you?
Darren: Maidstone. You?
Jasmine: Plymouth.
Darren: Long way.
Jasmine: Everyone says that. What do you do?
Darren: Bins. Loader on the council rounds.
Jasmine: Oh, okay. I've got two bubble tea shops, and honestly, our bins are a nightmare. Commercial waste is so expensive. I had to haggle the contract down last year, they wanted to put it up like fifteen percent.
Darren: Did you get it down?
Jasmine: To about six. I said I'd go somewhere else. I wouldn't have, but they didn't know that.
Darren: Fair play.
Jasmine: Is it the same for you, the commercial ones?
Darren: Nah, I'm domestic. Houses. Six o'clock start, same rounds eleven years.
Jasmine: Eleven years, wow. You must know every house.
Darren: I know which ones put rubbish in the recycling. That's most of them.
Jasmine: My staff do that. The cups with the plastic seal on top, they just chuck them in with the cardboard. I keep telling them.
Darren: That's exactly it. Then the whole bin gets rejected and they ring up and say we never took it. Half the time I'll stand there and pick the bits out myself so the whole street doesn't get marked down, and nobody thanks you for that, mate.
Jasmine: No, nobody thanks you. Same with running a shop, to be fair. Saturdays, someone always calls in sick. Every Saturday.
Darren: Never missed a start, me.
Jasmine: Seriously? In eleven years?
Darren: Not once.
Jasmine: Can I hire you?
Darren: Ha. Don't think I'd be any good at bubble tea.
Jasmine: You'd be fine. It's just pressing buttons, honestly. My partner Tom's like you, though. Just gets on with it. He's a marine engineer at Devonport.
Darren: Sensible bloke.
Jasmine: He is. Do you have family?
Darren: Partner, Tracey. And the dog, Roxy. Staffie. She's getting on now. Bad hips.
Jasmine: Oh no. Vet bills?
Darren: Don't. Every month something.
Jasmine: We've got a cat, Biscuit. She's fine, she just knocks everything off the counter. Do you go on holiday much?
Darren: Caravan in Norfolk. Benidorm every couple of years 'cause Tracey likes it. I can't stand airports.
Jasmine: I don't mind airports if I can sit in the lounge. I fly home to Malaysia via Doha, it's a long one. But I like Tenerife, all-inclusive, pool, done.
Darren: Yeah, see, that's what Tracey would want.
Jasmine: She's right, lah. You don't have to do anything.
Darren: Except queue for two hours at Gatwick.
Jasmine: Bristol's quicker, for me anyway. Or Exeter.
Darren: I'll mention it. She won't listen, mind.

=== CALL C0069 ===
Jasmine: Hi, can you hear me?
Bianca: Yeah. Hiya.
Jasmine: Jasmine. I'm in Plymouth.
Bianca: Bianca. Wolverhampton.
Jasmine: What do you do, Bianca?
Bianca: Erm, I'm at uni. Accounting and Finance, second year.
Jasmine: Oh, good. I need more accountants in my life. I've got two bubble tea shops and I do the books myself in Xero.
Bianca: Oh, we did Xero in a module last term. It's alright actually. Easier than Sage.
Jasmine: Much easier. My accountant still charges me like I'm making it hard for him, though.

Jasmine: Good. That's the right attitude. Where do you want to work?
Bianca: Birmingham, hopefully. I'm applying for placements at the mid-size firms. Then ACCA. I want to be earning properly by like twenty-five. Actual money, do you know what I mean.
Jasmine: You will. Accountants always have work, that's why I like them. Boring is good, you know. Boring pays.
Bianca: Yeah, that's literally what I told my mum.
Bianca: How did you get two shops, though? Like, at your age.
Jasmine: Savings, a loan from my dad, and my partner signed as guarantor. First one in 2019, second in 2022. My dad still talks about the loan like he owns the business. Every phone call it's "how's my shop?" It's not your shop, I paid you back.
Bianca: That's so annoying.
Jasmine: It is. Anyway. What do you do when you're not studying?
Bianca: Gym, mostly. Just the treadmill with my headphones in. I like that nobody talks to you.
Jasmine: Same, exactly the same. If someone tries to chat to me at PureGym I just point at my earphones.
Bianca: Yeah. And TV. Reality stuff. I'm on the new Married at First Sight Australia.
Jasmine: Oh my God, the Australian one is the best one. The British one is so boring compared.
Bianca: The Australian ones are proper unhinged.
Jasmine: Totally. Do you do skincare? You look like you do skincare.
Bianca: Yeah, a bit. I got this vitamin C serum half price last week off a discount code. Some Korean brand.
Jasmine: Which one? I buy mostly Korean and Japanese. Half price is good.
Bianca: I can't remember the name, it's got like an orange label. I use Vinted a lot as well. People sell stuff they've only opened once.
Jasmine: I sell on Vinted! I sold a coat last month for more than I paid. Forty-five pounds, and I got it for thirty in a sale.
Bianca: That's profit, that is.
Jasmine: That's what I said to Tom. He said I should declare it.
Bianca: Nobody declares Vinted, do you know what I mean.
Jasmine: Exactly, lah. Don't tell my accountant.
Bianca: I won't. Not yet, anyway.

Lee: Do you get back to see your family much? Living in the flat.
Bianca: My mum's only fifteen minutes away. She sends me home with loads of food every time. Like, tubs and tubs.
Lee: My wife does that with Megan. Puts a cob in her bag for the train.
Bianca: A cob?
Lee: Bread roll.
Bianca: Oh, we say bap. My mum sends soup, mostly. Romanian stuff.
Lee: Well, she won't go hungry, then.
Bianca: No. I've got a freezer full.
calls.C0072:
Darren: Alright. Can you hear me?
Gareth: Yeah, fine. Gareth.
Darren: Darren.
Gareth: Where are you, then?
Darren: Maidstone.
Gareth: Oh, not far. I grew up in Bromley. Sister's in Sevenoaks now.
Darren: Yeah? Sevenoaks. Bit posh for me.
Gareth: Bit posh for her, to be honest. What d'you do?
Darren: Bins. Council rounds. Six o'clock start.
Gareth: Fair enough. I'm a structural engineer. Office in Farringdon, but I'm out on sites a fair bit.
Darren: Hard hat and a clipboard.
Gareth: Pretty much, yeah. Mostly I'm telling contractors what they can't do.
Darren: Bet they love you.
Gareth: Er, some of them. A couple have asked for someone else, to be fair.
Darren: I tell supervisors straight as well. Doesn't make you popular.
Gareth: No. Gets the job done, though.
Darren: That's what I say.
Gareth: Football?
Darren: Gillingham.
Gareth: Ah. Palace, me.
Darren: You've got nothing to moan about, then.
Gareth: I've got plenty. Manager should've gone in about October. We just sit there drawing nil-nil every other week and everyone acts like that's fine.
Darren: Try watching us. You'd want nil-nil.
Gareth: Fair. D'you play?
Darren: Used to. Sunday league, when I was younger. Darts now. Pub league, Thursdays.
Gareth: I played five-a-side every Wednesday till I did my knee in at thirty-nine. Still plays up when it's cold.
Darren: My back's the same. Lifting bins all day. Dunno how long it'll last, to be honest.
Gareth: Can you move off the lifting?
Darren: Driving, if they put me through my HGV. They keep saying they will.
Gareth: Keep on at them.
Darren: Yeah. I will.
Gareth: Do you get a pint after the darts, then?
Darren: Couple of lagers. Price keeps going up though. Nearly six quid at my local.
Gareth: Six? That's cheap. Try Walthamstow. And everything's craft, so it's seven-fifty for a pale ale in a jam jar.
Darren: I don't see the point of craft beer. It's just lager that costs more.
Gareth: Nah, it's not, mate. Some of it's decent.
Darren: Some of it tastes like grapefruit.
Gareth: Yeah, alright, some of it does. My GP says I should drink less anyway.
Darren: Mine says it every time. I just nod.
Gareth: Same. Nod, and then—

C0069.line_text: Bianca: I can't remember the name, it's got like an orange label. I use Vinted a lot as well. People sell stuff they've only opened once.
C0069.what: A young man in a dark work polo, sleepy-looking, walks across the room behind Bianca, unplugs the phone charger trailing over the settee arm and walks back out of frame. Bianca doesn't turn round and keeps talking.
